description.value: Speech struck with the plate edge of the fused skull against wet rock, because nothing vocal survives the rain on a windward crest. Range is a few hundred metres and the syntax is dense, with tense, presence and intention folded into single figures. It has no first person that can be held by one body: a knocked statement is attributable to the crest and not to a speaker, which is why property claims in this culture will not resolve and why the survey's consent forms had to be redesigned twice. The usual first error is to take the whole thing for a set of fixed calls, since the commonest twenty figures cover most of an ordinary day and can be listed in an afternoon.

sampleGloss.value: (two knocks, a pause of one beat, four fast knocks) - here, not-yet, going - somebody is on this crest and is leaving it, and the two facts are one word.

note.value: Recorded during elicitation and kept as the reference sample for this system.
